title: at 8 o'clock on Monday in April
subtitle: at / on / in for time
summary: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, and in for months, years and seasons.

lesson.heading: at / on / in
rows: on Monday, on 25 April, on New Year's Day

lesson.heading: at + clock times
lesson.text: We use **at** with the time on the clock. We also use **at** in some other time expressions: **at night**, **at the weekend**, **at Christmas**, **at Easter**, **at the end of** ..., **at the moment**.

examples.text: Are you going away **at the weekend**?

lesson.note: We say **at Christmas**, but **on** Christmas **Day**. We also say: I'm going on holiday **at the end of** October.

lesson.heading: on + days and dates
lesson.text: We use **on** with days of the week and with dates.

examples.text: What do you usually do **on Sundays**?

lesson.heading: in + months, years and seasons
lesson.text: We use **in** with months, years and seasons - longer periods of time.

lesson.heading: in the morning / on Monday morning

left.label: in the morning / in the evening
left.text: Use in with a part of the day alone.
examples: I always feel good **in the morning**.
Do you often go out **in the evening**?

right.label: on Monday morning / on Saturday night
right.text: Use on when you say the day too.
examples: Are you doing anything **on Saturday night**?

lesson.note: But we say **at night**: I can't sleep at night.

lesson.heading: No at / on / in before this, last, next, every
lesson.text: We do **not** use at, on or in before **this** ..., **last** ..., **next** ... and **every** ... .

examples.text: We go on holiday **every summer**. **Last summer** we went to Canada.

lesson.heading: in five minutes / in a few days
lesson.text: **in** + a period of time means 'from now'. **in five minutes** = five minutes from now.

examples.text: Hurry! The train leaves **in five minutes**.
Bye! I'll see you **in a few days**.

exercises.prompt: I got up ___ 8 o'clock this morning.
exercises.explanation: We use at with clock times.
We use on with days of the week.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with each time expression?
I like getting up early ___ the morning.
exercises.explanation: in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening.

exercises.prompt: I'll send you the money ___ the end of the month.
exercises.explanation: We say at the end of ... .

exercises.prompt: Did you go out ___ Tuesday evening?
exercises.explanation: When the day is there too, we use on: on Tuesday evening.

exercises.statement: We went to France last summer.
exercises.explanation: Correct. We do not use at, on or in before last ... .

exercises.prompt: Lisa's diary for next week says: Wednesday - cinema (evening). Lisa is going to the cinema ___.
exercises.explanation: The day is there too, so we use on: on Wednesday evening.
I'm leaving next Monday. We do not use on before next ... .

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: Are you going away at the weekend?

exercises.prompt: It's 8.25 now and the train leaves at 8.30. The train leaves ___.
exercises.explanation: in + a period of time means 'from now': in five minutes.
